name: Toyota Logistics Services Vehicle Distribution Center - Newark NJ

fieldNotes.facilityType: Port Newark auto-processing terminal operated by Toyota Logistics Services (Toyota Motor Logistics Center), Building 390 E Port St. One of three vehicle processors at the Port of New York/New Jersey (alongside FAPS and BMW Port Jersey). Vehicles arrive by ro/ro vessel at the wharf, are processed (accessory install, recon, PDI) and distributed by auto-hauler truck and rail to the eastern US.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Port Newark is a TWIC-controlled marine terminal — controlled gated entry is certain. The facility is fenced (chain-link visible in Street View along E Port St) with vehicle lots and processing buildings inside. E Port St frontage gives a controlled entrance to the processing complex.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true. A small gatehouse-type structure sits at the SE corner near where E Port St meets the facility. TWIC marine terminals are staffed at the gate. A discrete booth could not be isolated frame-by-frame; medium confidence.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed — rail tracks run along E Port St adjacent to the facility (visible in Street View) and Port Newark's auto terminals are served by on-dock rail. TLS distributes vehicles inland by rail.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: The processing complex includes a large sawtooth-roof building and an adjacent flat-roof building with dock-style doors for parts/accessory and auto-hauler loading; banded 10-25. Atypical metric for a vehicle-processing site.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Vast — the facility is dominated by striped vehicle marshalling lots holding thousands of finished vehicles, plus a dense yard of auto-haulers/tractors and trailers (~45 visible in z20 imagery); banded 50+.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: z20 imagery shows a packed yard of tractors, trailers and auto-hauler units — estimated ~45 visible; high truck activity.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; left false, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons and multiple yard lanes give room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: At least one main E Port St gate; a secondary access likely — estimated 2, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box ~58 acres covering the TLS processing buildings and contiguous vehicle lots fronting E Port St between the Port Newark Channel wharf and the rail corridor.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Within the Port Newark/Elizabeth marine-terminal complex in the New York metro; classified Urban.
